concepts.definition: Synthesis is the process of synthesizing parts to form complete realistic imagery.

concepts.name: generic graphics system
concepts.definition: A generic graphics system is a conceptual model used to identify the major components and basic terms required to understand the process of rendering.

concepts.name: display controller
concepts.definition: This component sends data to video memory for storage and communicates with the CPU.

concepts.name: video memory
concepts.definition: This component stores data that is sent by the display controller.

concepts.name: video controller
concepts.definition: This component utilizes data from video memory to render an image on the screen.

concepts.name: Graphics card
concepts.definition: It is a dedicated component of the system that deals with rendering-related computations.

concepts.name: Image generation
concepts.definition: It is the process of rendering a scene on the screen, which is nothing but a 2D image displayed on a 2D screen.

concepts.name: Pixels
concepts.definition: Pixels are the picture elements that are arranged in a grid on a graphic display screen.

concepts.name: Vector scan device
concepts.definition: A graphic device that renders an image by activating only selective pixels that represent continuous geometric primitives, such as lines or curves.

concepts.name: Raster scan device
concepts.definition: A graphic device that renders an image by considering all pixels in the whole pixel grid, not only the selected pixels representing primitives.

concepts.name: Geometric primitives
concepts.definition: Basic geometric shapes, such as lines or curves, that an image is viewed as being composed of in a vector scan device.

concepts.name: Scanning or raster scanning
concepts.definition: The process of activating all pixels in sequence, typically from left to right, top to bottom, to achieve overall perception.

concepts.name: Raster scan displays
concepts.definition: Raster scan displays are typically found in commercial products, such as smartphones or televisions, and their rendering mechanism is much cheaper compared to the selective rendering required for vector scan devices.

concepts.name: Frame buffer
concepts.definition: The frame buffer is the video memory component of a raster scan system that stores the intensity values for all pixels in the grid.

concepts.name: Screen refreshing
concepts.definition: Refreshing is the process of periodically exciting the pixels, even if the image is not changing, to ensure uniformity in the rendered image.

concepts.name: Refresh rate
concepts.definition: The refresh rate is the number of times a scene is refreshed per second on the screen.

concepts.name: Image distortion
concepts.definition: Image distortion is a potential visual artifact where the final image may not appear uniform or may appear distorted because pixels are excited and decay at different points in time.

concepts.name: Color screens or color displays
concepts.definition: Each pixel contains more than one type of element.

concepts.name: Primary colors
concepts.definition: These typically represent red, green, and blue.

concepts.name: 3D computer graphics pipeline
concepts.definition: It refers to the process of computation starting from object representation to rendering on the pixel grid.

concepts.name: Graphics pipeline
concepts.definition: The stages together that are known as the graphics pipeline, which computes the values stored in the frame buffer.

concepts.name: Display processor
concepts.definition: The display processor is responsible for computing the real number values stored in the framebuffer in distinct stages.

concepts.name: Object representation
concepts.definition: This is the first stage where objects that will constitute the image on display are defined.

concepts.name: Modeling transformation
concepts.definition: This second stage transforms objects from their local coordinate system definition to objects in the world coordinate system definition.

concepts.name: Lighting stage
concepts.definition: This third stage involves assigning color to the objects after the 3D scene has been constructed.

concepts.name: Viewing transformation
concepts.definition: This fourth stage maps the colored 3D scene from the world coordinate system to 2D device coordinates, simulating a camera snapshot.

concepts.name: Scan conversion
concepts.definition: This fifth stage transforms the continuous device coordinate space description into a discrete pixel grid description.

concepts.name: World coordinate system
concepts.definition: This is the common coordinate system used to put together multiple objects defined in their own local coordinate systems to construct the overall image.

concepts.name: Balance
concepts.definition: The objective of having a representation that captures all intricate details while maintaining efficient subsequent computation.

concepts.name: Point sample rendering
concepts.definition: This technique captures information in the form of points on the scene, where each point carries specific attributes.

concepts.name: Boundary representation
concepts.definition: Objects are represented by the surfaces that define the boundary of the object.

concepts.name: Space partitioning representation
concepts.definition: The 3D space occupied by the object is divided into several disjoint or non-overlapping regions.

concepts.name: Spline representation
concepts.definition: This method represents curves or curved surfaces using several lower-degree polynomials instead of a single complex polynomial.

concepts.name: Fractal representation
concepts.definition: This is a specialized way to represent structures that are self-repeating, where each part repeats in the larger part.

concepts.name: Object representation technique
concepts.definition: This is the first stage of the 3D graphics pipeline that was discussed in the lecture.

concepts.name: Object representation
concepts.definition: This is the first stage of the pipeline, which happens in the local coordinate system.

concepts.name: Viewing pipeline
concepts.definition: This is the fourth stage, which contains several sub-stages starting with viewing transformation.

concepts.name: Projection transformation
concepts.definition: This transformation converts the scene from a 3D view coordinate to a 2D view coordinate system.

concepts.name: Local or object coordinate system description
concepts.definition: This is the individual definition of an object, where its position, dimension, and other properties are defined relative to the object itself.

concepts.name: Basic transformations
concepts.definition: These are the fundamental operations—translation, rotation, scaling, and shearing—that can be combined to create any required transformation.

concepts.name: Homogeneous coordinate system
concepts.definition: This is a setting where the matrix representation of transformations is typically performed, allowing for the inclusion of an extra dimension.

concepts.name: Composite transformation matrix
concepts.definition: This matrix is obtained by multiplying multiple basic transformation matrices together to represent a sequence of operations.

concepts.name: Color computation
concepts.definition: This is the process of assigning colors to the objects in the scene, which is necessary for perceiving depth.

concepts.name: Lighting model
concepts.definition: A model that computes colors in terms of continuous intensity values and involves more computation compared to shading models.

concepts.name: Shading model
concepts.definition: A method used to reduce computation while approximating color assignment without compromising the quality of experience.

concepts.name: Continuous intensity values
concepts.definition: These are real numbers, typically within the range 0 to 1, that lighting models use to compute colors.

concepts.name: Diffuse light component
concepts.definition: The diffuse light component is light that comes directly from the source and is reflected in a diffuse manner.

concepts.name: Specular reflection component
concepts.definition: The specular reflection component is light that comes from the source and is reflected with a shiny bright spot effect.

concepts.name: Reflection coefficient
concepts.definition: The reflection coefficient, or reflectivity, is a surface property that determines the fraction of incident light that gets reflected and comes to the viewer's eye.

concepts.name: Phi
concepts.definition: Phi is the angle between the viewer direction and the ideal specular reflection direction.

concepts.name: Ideal specular reflection direction
concepts.definition: The ideal specular reflection direction (r) is the direction of the reflected light if the surface were a mirror.

concepts.name: Radial intensity attenuation
concepts.definition: This factor accounts for the effect of diminishing light intensity over distance, typically computed using an inverse quadratic function.

concepts.name: Angular intensity attenuation
concepts.definition: This factor is considered when generating spotlight effects, where the intensity varies based on the angle relative to the light source.

concepts.name: Attenuation factor
concepts.definition: This factor is used to modify the light source intensity, causing it to change based on the distance or angle of the surface point from the light source.

concepts.name: Colored light model
concepts.definition: The colored light model is a slightly different way of thinking about assigning colors.

concepts.name: Source intensity
concepts.definition: The source intensity is a three-element vector (Isr, Isg, Isb) corresponding to the three primary colors.

concepts.name: IP
concepts.definition: IP is the resulting intensity calculated when considering ambient light plus the summation of contributions from multiple light sources.

concepts.name: Transformation matrix
concepts.definition: This is an individual basic or composite matrix used to transform a point from its local coordinate system to the world coordinate system.

concepts.name: Composite matrix
concepts.definition: This is a matrix that is more common and is used to multiply the point vector to determine the transformed point.

concepts.name: Mapping table
concepts.definition: This is a device-specific table that stores device intensities and their corresponding bit patterns.

concepts.name: Object representation
concepts.definition: Object representation is the first stage of the pipeline that takes place in the local coordinate reference frame.

concepts.name: Lighting calculation
concepts.definition: Lighting calculation is the third stage of the pipeline, which takes place in the world coordinate scene.

concepts.name: Projection
concepts.definition: Projection is the process of selecting a portion of a 3D scene and transforming it from 3D space onto a 2D display plane or view plane.

concepts.name: Projection transformation
concepts.definition: A projection transformation is the specific transformation that converts data from 3D space to a 2D screen.

concepts.name: window-to-viewport transformation
concepts.definition: This transformation converts a 2D view plane description of the scene into a 2D device coordinate space.

concepts.name: clipping
concepts.definition: Clipping is an operation that takes place in the 3D view coordinate system.

concepts.name: hidden surface removal
concepts.definition: Hidden surface removal is an operation that takes place in the 3D view coordinate system.

concepts.name: View coordinate system
concepts.definition: This system has its own axes (u, n, and v) and is used to transfer a point from the world coordinate to the 3D view coordinate scene.

concepts.name: Orthogonal axes
concepts.definition: These are the three mutually orthogonal axes (N, V, and U) that together define the view coordinate system.

concepts.name: Camera position
concepts.definition: The camera position serves as the origin vector with respect to the world coordinate scene.

concepts.name: View plane
concepts.definition: The view plane is typically defined as a rectangular area.

concepts.name: View volume
concepts.definition: A 3D region in the scene that defines the portion of the scene that is going to be projected onto the view plane.

concepts.name: Clipping process
concepts.definition: The process of discarding objects that are outside of the defined view volume but are part of the scene.

concepts.name: Parallel projection
concepts.definition: A type of projection where the projectors are parallel to each other, meaning the center of projection is at infinity.

concepts.name: Canonical view volume
concepts.definition: A canonical view volume is a concept used to simplify pipeline computations.

concepts.name: Normalized cube
concepts.definition: It is a cube used to define the view volume, converting any arbitrary view volume into a standard shape.

concepts.name: Homogeneous factor w
concepts.definition: This is a factor, typically not equal to 1, that requires division to convert the obtained coordinate values into Cartesian points.

concepts.name: Window
concepts.definition: A window is the same as a normalized clipping window and is an abstract intermediate representation.

concepts.name: Viewport
concepts.definition: The viewport is defined in device space as a portion of the final screen where the scene will be rendered, specified by the screen or display origin and screen dimensions.

concepts.name: Projection transformation
concepts.definition: Transformation from 3D view coordinate to 2D view coordinate system.

concepts.name: Window to viewport transformation
concepts.definition: Transforming from 2D view coordinate system to a device coordinate system.

concepts.name: Device coordinate system
concepts.definition: This is a continuous coordinate system where the coordinate values can be any real number.

concepts.name: Pixel grid
concepts.definition: This is the structure of the display device used to render the image, where points must have integer coordinates.

concepts.name: Discrete coordinate system
concepts.definition: This is a coordinate system where the coordinates can only be integer values, as required by the pixel grid.

concepts.name: Rasterization
concepts.definition: This is the process of mapping from the continuous viewport space to the discrete pixel grid space, often called rendering or scan conversion.

concepts.name: Point rendering
concepts.definition: It is the process of rounding real coordinates to the nearest integer values to represent a point.

concepts.name: Line rendering
concepts.definition: It is one of the most common activities in image rendering, serving as the basis of any image rendering.

concepts.name: Bresenham's line drawing algorithm
concepts.definition: It is a popular algorithm used to find the pixels that approximately represent a line segment using only integer arithmetic.

concepts.name: Discrete space
concepts.definition: It is the space to which real coordinates are mapped by rounding them to nearest integer values.

concepts.name: Decision parameter
concepts.definition: It is a parameter used in Bresenham's algorithm, initially calculated as twice delta y minus delta x.

concepts.name: Anti-aliasing operations
concepts.definition: Anti-aliasing operations are additional processes used to remove or reduce the distortion caused by aliasing so that the end effect is better.

concepts.name: API
concepts.definition: APIs are predefined sets of functions that perform specific tasks when invoked with appropriate arguments or parameters.

concepts.name: Graphics library
concepts.definition: Graphics libraries are existing implementations that programmers can import to use APIs and handle graphics-related concerns.

concepts.name: Function
concepts.definition: A function, such as glColor3frgb, is used to assign colors to a 3D point.

concepts.name: VR application layer
concepts.definition: The VR application layer is positioned at the top of the layered architecture, situated above the software development kit (SDK) layer.

concepts.name: Native rendering libraries
concepts.definition: These libraries, such as OpenGL or Vulkan, are called by the VR engine to perform rendering activities.

concepts.name: Layered architecture
concepts.definition: This is the structural form used to understand the overall virtual reality system.

concepts.name: Hardware layer
concepts.definition: This is the bottom layer of the system, which includes the GPU.

concepts.name: Parallelism
concepts.definition: Parallelism is the need and ability to perform graphics operations, such as applying transformations to vertices, simultaneously to achieve a significant gain in performance.

concepts.name: Multicore systems
concepts.definition: Multicore systems are characterized by containing a large number of cores or unit processing elements.

concepts.name: Single instructions
concepts.definition: Single instructions is a method where all cores work simultaneously on an instruction and produce data simultaneously.

concepts.name: Streaming multiprocessor units
concepts.definition: Streaming multiprocessor units are formed when multiple cores group together within the GPU.

concepts.name: Texture storage
concepts.definition: Texture storage is an element that stores information about predefined colors, surface colors, or predetermined surface colors.

concepts.name: Streaming multiprocessor
concepts.definition: A streaming multiprocessor contains several streaming processors or cores.

concepts.name: Rasterization stage
concepts.definition: In the rasterization stage, pixels are determined based on how they overlap the device space triangle.

concepts.name: Depth buffer
concepts.definition: The depth buffer is a dedicated memory that stores the depth information for each point in a 3D scene before they are projected onto a 2D plane.

concepts.name: Combination of exploration techniques
concepts.definition: A combination of exploration techniques is a required method for the virtual tour.

concepts.name: Optimization technique
concepts.definition: Optimization techniques were required to address the challenges presented by the application's vast and complex content.

concepts.name: Standalone computing device
concepts.definition: A computing device that has its own processor and memory and does not need to be tethered to an external computer.

concepts.name: Optimization strategy
concepts.definition: A strategy used to reduce the size of the application and associated computations, including memory access.

concepts.name: Cloud computing-based approach
concepts.definition: A strategy where large data, such as videos, is stored externally in the cloud rather than locally on the client device.

concepts.name: Immersive environment
concepts.definition: An immersive environment is what you get to see when you wear the cardboard headset and create stereoscopic views.

concepts.name: Compression
concepts.definition: Compression is an optimization strategy that was implemented.

concepts.name: Storage requirements
concepts.definition: Storage requirements are reduced by compressing the images that are used in the system.

concepts.name: Rendering optimization
concepts.definition: Rendering optimization is the process of taking care of optimization concerns related to rendering.

concepts.name: Computational issues associated with rendering immersive experiences
concepts.definition: These are computational problems that require recourse to different approaches, such as using cloud-based services or employing compression techniques.

concepts.name: Link theory to practice
concepts.definition: This is the topic of the lecture, which discusses how to connect theoretical knowledge to practical implementation.

concepts.name: Unity platform
concepts.definition: It is a popular and well-known programming environment for developers who wish to work with extended reality systems, comprising the game engine, Unity 3D game engine, and a developer's interface.

concepts.name: Unity
concepts.definition: Unity is a cross-platform game engine initially released by Unity Technologies in 2005.

concepts.name: Unity Hub
concepts.definition: Unity Hub is a standalone application that streamlines the way you find, download and manage your Unity projects and installations.

concepts.name: Editor interface
concepts.definition: The editor interface allows you to build and deploy realistic immersive environment without having to master and implement the CG pipeline.

concepts.name: integrated development environment
concepts.definition: It is essentially an IDE providing the developer all the features required to build and deploy a system.

concepts.name: scene view
concepts.definition: It is component A, which is basically called the scene view.

concepts.name: game view
concepts.definition: It is component B, which refers to the game view.

concepts.name: Asset
concepts.definition: An asset is any item that is used in a Unity project to create the application.

concepts.name: Scene
concepts.definition: A scene is a specific type of asset that contains all or part of a game or application.

concepts.name: Game object
concepts.definition: These are fundamental objects that represent characters, props, or scenarios, and they act as containers for components that implement functionality.

concepts.name: Prefab
concepts.definition: Prefabs are templates that allow you to create, configure, and store game objects, which the user can then make instances of.

concepts.name: Component
concepts.definition: Components implement the functionality of an object and must be added to a game object to give it properties.

concepts.name: Unity developer environment
concepts.definition: This is an implementation platform that includes an editor interface allowing a developer to create, build, and deploy a system.

concepts.name: Render pipeline support
concepts.definition: This is important graphics support offered by Unity that allows the implementation of the entire graphics pipeline.

concepts.name: Built-in render pipeline
concepts.definition: This is one of the three pre-built render pipelines provided by Unity, which has limited options for customization.

concepts.name: Universal Render Pipeline
concepts.definition: This pipeline is quick and easy to customize and allows the creation of optimized graphics across a wide range of platforms.

concepts.name: High definition render pipeline
concepts.definition: The High Definition Render Pipeline (HDRP) is a customizable pipeline that enables the creation of cutting-edge, high-fidelity graphics on high-end platforms.

concepts.name: Custom render pipeline
concepts.definition: This is a render pipeline that a developer can create using Unity's scriptable render pipeline APIs.

concepts.name: Materials
concepts.definition: Materials describe the appearance of the surface, detailing how a surface should be rendered.

concepts.name: Textures
concepts.definition: Textures are bitmap images that are applied over the mesh surface to assign colors.

concepts.name: Models
concepts.definition: Models are files that contain data regarding the shape and appearance of 3D objects.

concepts.name: Object Definition
concepts.definition: Object definition is the first stage of the graphics pipeline that supports how an object is defined.

concepts.name: 3D Meshes
concepts.definition: 3D meshes are the main graphics primitives of Unity.

concepts.name: Skybox
concepts.definition: A skybox is a cube with different textures on its faces used to create a 360-degree environment.

concepts.name: Shadow mapping
concepts.definition: Shadow mapping is a technique used to render real-time shadows.

concepts.name: Halo effect
concepts.definition: The halo effect is a visual effect that creates light areas around light sources.

concepts.name: Line renderer effect
concepts.definition: The line renderer effect takes an array of two or more points in 3D space and draws a straight line between those points.

concepts.name: View transformation or viewing pipeline
concepts.definition: This is an important stage in the 3D graphics pipeline.

concepts.name: Camera
concepts.definition: A camera allows a developer to set up a view, and the system performs other calculations accordingly.

concepts.name: Layered architecture of an XR system
concepts.definition: The structural organization of an XR system, which ranges from the application layer down to the hardware, including the GPU.

concepts.name: Unity's default graphics APIs
concepts.definition: APIs provided by Unity that access the underlying library APIs, allowing developers to use Unity's default graphics.

concepts.name: AutoGraphics API
concepts.definition: A feature that, when checked, ensures the player build uses a set of built-in graphics APIs and selects the appropriate one at runtime for the best scenario.

concepts.name: Rigid body
concepts.definition: A property that, when attached to a game object, allows the game object to respond to gravity.

concepts.name: Colliders
concepts.definition: Defines the shape of a game object for the purpose of physical collisions.

concepts.name: Joints
concepts.definition: Connects a rigid body to another rigid body or to a fixed point in space, and can apply forces that move the rigid bodies.

concepts.name: Articulation
concepts.definition: The realistic physics behavior that involves joints, describing how the overall structure comprising joints moves.

concepts.name: Humanoid animation retargeting
concepts.definition: This is the ability to apply animations from one character model onto another.

concepts.name: Audio listener
concepts.definition: It listens to all audio playing in the scene and transfers it to the computer speakers.

concepts.name: Audio filters
concepts.definition: These components output the audio source after some modification, allowing for various sound effects.

concepts.name: Scripting support
concepts.definition: Scripting support is an important component of a development environment that provides crucial programming support for a more customized experience.

concepts.name: Unity game engine
concepts.definition: The Unity game engine is the middleware that is automatically installed when the Unity Hub package is installed.

concepts.name: Middleware
concepts.definition: Middleware is the type of software that the Unity game engine is.

concepts.name: Script
concepts.definition: A script is essentially a new type of component that can be attached to game objects.

concepts.name: Inheritance
concepts.definition: Inheritance is the process where the MonoBehaviour class is inherited by the class being defined.

concepts.name: Start function
concepts.definition: The Start function is called whenever the script is called and serves as the starting point of the script.

concepts.name: Update function
concepts.definition: The Update function is invoked in each frame whenever the script executes and some change happens.

concepts.name: Vector3
concepts.definition: Vector3 is a data type used to represent a position of a 3D point by capturing three coordinates.

concepts.name: Debug.Log function
concepts.definition: The Debug.Log function is used to print a message onto the console output.

concepts.name: Destroying an object
concepts.definition: This is the process of removing a game object from the scene, supported by the scripting environment.

concepts.name: Destroy function
concepts.definition: A function under the MonoBehaviour class that can be attached to a game object to specify a time after which it should be destroyed.

concepts.name: Parameters
concepts.definition: Inputs that are given to a function each time it is called.

concepts.name: User-defined functions
concepts.definition: Functions that are typically part of a good script and are created by the programmer.

concepts.name: Event functions
concepts.definition: Functions that are activated by Unity in response to events that occur during gameplay.

concepts.name: Trigger
concepts.definition: A configuration applied to a collider that causes specific physics-related events to be called.

concepts.name: Event handler or event function
concepts.definition: When an event occurs, control is passed to the event handler or function, and the function body is then executed.

concepts.name: Instantiating prefabs at runtime
concepts.definition: This is the process where the code or script must have a reference to a prefab in order to create it during runtime.

concepts.name: Conditional statements
concepts.definition: These are standard programming constructs that allow the script to execute different code based on whether a specific condition is met.

concepts.name: Entry-controlled loops
concepts.definition: These loops, such as for or while, set and check the loop conditions at the beginning before the loop body executes.

concepts.name: Exit-controlled loop
concepts.definition: This type of loop, such as do while, ensures the loop body is evaluated at least one time because the testing condition is checked at the end.

concepts.name: For each loop
concepts.definition: This loop is used for arrays or collections of homogeneous data types, allowing the programmer to directly use the data without dealing with individual data types.

concepts.name: Transform property
concepts.definition: A property attached to every game object that is used to store and manipulate the object's position, rotation, and scale.

concepts.name: Coroutines
concepts.definition: A method that allows a developer to pause execution and return control to Unity, but then continue where it left off on the following frame, spreading tasks across several frames.

concepts.name: InvokeRepeating
concepts.definition: A function that invokes a method at a specific time and then repeatedly calls it every specified second.

concepts.name: Scripting
concepts.definition: Scripting supports user interaction with input devices.

concepts.name: Immersive environment
concepts.definition: A key aspect of any immersive environment is that the user should be able to interact.

concepts.name: SDKs
concepts.definition: SDKs are imported to provide device-specific input support that extends the inbuilt support of Unity.

concepts.name: Scenes in Build panel
concepts.definition: The Scenes in Build panel is used to manage which scenes are included in the build.

concepts.name: Platform section
concepts.definition: The platform section is used to select which platform the system will be built or deployed to.

concepts.name: SDKs or packages
concepts.definition: These are imported packages that allow a developer to access or utilize specific functions and functionalities provided by specified hardware or software platforms.

concepts.name: Vuforia
concepts.definition: Vuforia is an SDK primarily designed to help developers deal with object recognition or computer vision issues, such as object detection, recognition, and tracking.

concepts.name: Database
concepts.definition: This database is required for the recognition task and is used to store images that the Vuforia engine needs to recognize.

concepts.name: Image target
concepts.definition: This is the image that is added to the database and which the Vuforia engine attempts to recognize for the AR application.

concepts.name: Vuforia engine
concepts.definition: It can add image recognition functionalities to the built-in environment.

concepts.name: device-specific SDKs
concepts.definition: These are utilized to access device-specific data, sensory data, or input data.

concepts.name: building and deployment
concepts.definition: Building and deployment are primarily programming tasks.

concepts.name: functionalities
concepts.definition: These are features that can be supported by the development environment or in conjunction with other SDKs.

concepts.name: Interdisciplinary
concepts.definition: Interdisciplinary means that a field takes input from multiple disciplines.

concepts.name: LLM
concepts.definition: LLM stands for large language models, which can be utilized for enhanced interactivity.

concepts.name: Generative AI
concepts.definition: Generative AI is a concept that can be utilized for enhanced interactivity.
